title: Base-linear exceptional transpose and exact tower detection
statement: For closed structures SA and SC and a coefficient pairing frame F [def-coef-tower-evaluation-pairing-constructions], define the base pairing by proper projection, inverse open tensor comparison, source counit and evaluation. Given a base trace P(J(Q)) → U, define its exceptional map by the closed transpose over the base, followed by the base-sections adjunction. The pairing is dinatural in M, so the exceptional maps are contravariantly natural. For strict scalar-module derived towers define exact level evaluation and prove that these evaluations jointly detect invertibility.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: The proper projection mate is natural in both variables, by its construction as a natural transformation. The open tensor inverse is natural by its prescribed adjunct. Source-counit naturality and closed evaluation dinaturality therefore prove base-pairing dinaturality.
Apply the closed Hom equivalence and the sections adjunction Hom equivalence to that equality to obtain naturality of the exceptional map.
Commute exact evaluation with homology. A homology arrow is a tower natural transformation and is invertible if all components are. Derived homology jointly detects isomorphisms.
